observations: English could_not_apply context note now reads 'suppresses countdown when apply_outcome is not retryable (false or absent)'. Verified against code by executing hasPermanentCredentialOutcome on parsed rows: stored retryable false -> permanent; retryable ABSENT inside a present apply_outcome -> permanent (applyOutcome normalises retryable === true); retryable true -> not permanent; a fresh refusal carrying an outcome without retryable overrides a stored true -> permanent; a no-outcome refusal keeps the stored value. The tray renders could_not_apply in place of approved_not_applied and gates the countdown on !permanentOutcome; canDenyApproval keeps Cancel sharing on approved/failed. Accurate. Wording caveat, not counted: a row with NO apply_outcome object at all is not permanent; '(false or absent)' is meant as retryable false or absent, which is how a translator reads it in context. No translation affected.
